text:
alex.d: FYI — our Windows CI boxes started failing node streaming tests this morning with TLS verification errors. stack: node 18, WSL2 Ubuntu, corporate proxy in the middle.

maria: ugh same. local dev on macs fine, only windows images. error is `UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE` from Node's TLS.

tyler: can you paste the exact curl/openssl output? often it's missing the corp CA in the WSL cert store.

alex.d: here's `curl -v https://api.redwood.dev/v1/health` snippet: "* SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'api.redwood.dev'
* CAfile: none CRLfile: none
* Unable to use client certificate (no key found or wrong format)
* SSL: certificate subject name 'CorpProxy Inc' matched" then `curl` exits with 60.

jen: that sounds like the MITM proxy is presenting its cert. In corp environments you need to add the proxy CA to the distro's trust store inside WSL.

maria: tried copying the corp root cert to `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/corp-root.crt` and ran `sudo update-ca-certificates` — still failing for node streaming tests (same error).

tyler: check Node's CA handling. Node does not automatically read the distro NSS certs in some builds. try exporting `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` before running the tests.

alex.d: tried that too, no dice. Also tried `export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`. Node server still rejects during TLS handshake.

infra-bot: build 5428 failed — mocha integration: streaming-auth.spec.js — TLS handshake error.

jen: two more things to try: 1) verify the cert chain with openssl to see if proxy is stripping intermediates: `openssl s_client -showcerts -connect api.redwood.dev:443 -servername api.redwood.dev` 2) make sure Windows host has the CA in the Windows cert store AND WSL is using same file (sometimes copying from Windows to WSL needed).

alex.d: openssl output shows only one cert (CorpProxy CA) — no chain back to a public root. looks like proxy re-signing.

maria: for Firefox you might need `certutil` and add to the NSS DB: `certutil -A -n "Corp Proxy Root" -t TC -d sql:$HOME/.pki/nssdb -i corp-root.crt`

tyler: another gotcha: some CI images use a static Node build compiled with OpenSSL statically linked and a different default certificate bundle path. check `node -p "require('tls').DEFAULT_CERT_STORE"` (not always present) or `process.versions.openssl`. For our images, easiest reliable route is to set `NODE_OPTIONS='--use-openssl-ca'` on newer Node builds or use `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` with the direct path to the corp root.

alex.d: hmm `process.versions.openssl` shows 3.0.7; I tried `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-openssl-ca`, test runner ignores it (mocha spawns subprocesses).

jen: if test harness spawns children, export it in the environment that launches CI agents (in the Dockerfile or the pipeline job). For ephemeral test containers, add the cert to image's `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` so builds are reproducible.

maria: question — why do macs work then? how do devs not see this?

tyler: macOS and our mac CI use the system keychain which the corp MDM auto-populates. Windows has its own store and WSL uses separate cert files unless you explicitly sync. Docker images are independent too.

alex.d: test: I copied corp-root.crt to a scratch Dockerfile based on ubuntu:22.04 and ran `update-ca-certificates` — `curl` works in container but Node still fails in same container.

jen: if Node still fails in container after system CA update, confirm Node process actually sees the file. run `node -e "console.log(process.env.NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, process.env.SSL_CERT_FILE)"` inside container. Also run `node -e "require('https').get('https://api.redwood.dev', res => console.log('ok'), err => console.error(err))"` to reproduce.

alex.d: output shows NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS is unset. when I set it `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt node ...` then the standalone HTTPS GET works. BUT our streaming client (using http2 and `fetch` polyfill + retry logic) still fails intermittently with `certificate verify failed` during chunked responses.

tyler: streaming + proxies sometimes mess with connection reuse and SNI. Add `--no-keepalive` small test? Also try forcing ALPN to `http/1.1` to see if http2 layer is the issue.

maria: quick test: `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=... node -e "const http2 = require('http2'); const c = http2.connect('https://api.redwood.dev'); c.on('error', console.error);"` gives same cert error.

jen: last resort debugging steps: 1) run `tcpdump` to capture TLS handshake, 2) run `openssl s_client` from within Node container namespace to compare, 3) try a minimal reproducible script that uses `https.request` (no http2) to isolate.

alex.d: capturing pcap shows the proxy rewrites cert on initial handshake — so chain unknown to Node. I can add the corp root to `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` in pipeline but need a durable fix for devs and CI.

jen: ops/security policy usually says we should distribute corp root via the company bootstrap scripts or the CI image base. @security can confirm official distribution channel.

security: pls open a ticket with IT cert ops. We can add the corp CA to the internal CA bundle artifact that images pull on startup. Don't set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` in CI — bad practice.

maria: I'll file a ticket and link here. For immediate unblocking I'll bake the cert into the test image and export `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` in the pipeline env.

alex.d: thanks — will try that approach and report back. if anyone has a one-liner to import corp cert into WSL from Windows automatically, lemme know.

tyler: one-liner (power shell): `certutil -addstore -f "Root" C:\path\to\corp-root.crt; wsl -u root -- sh -c "cp /mnt/c/path/to/corp-root.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ && update-ca-certificates"` — requires admin on Windows.

maria: perfect. saved. :thumbsup:

alex.d: closing the loop — baked into image and CI passes now. will keep ticket open for official distribution. thanks everyone.
